# Requirement
```text
Online Rideshare System (ORS) manages shared road trips between drivers and customers. Every user is identified by an id and also stores an email address and a phone number so that the platform can distinguish and contact the user.

A driver can publish trips. A trip records a departure station, an arrival station, the number of available seats, a departure date, a departure time, an arrival time, and a price. Trips can be direct or indirect. An indirect trip contains one or more stops, and each stop stores the name of its stop station.

A customer can create bookings for trips. A booking records the requested number of seats, the booking date, the related customer, and the related trip. A booking is valid only when the trip exists, enough seats are still available, the customer has no overlapping booking on the same day, and the booking is made more than two hours before the trip departure time. When a booking is accepted, the trip seat inventory must be reduced accordingly.

Customers may subscribe to a membership package. A membership package stores one or more rewards, and each reward is one of cashback, discounts, or points. A customer with a discount reward receives a 20 percent discount only when the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure. A customer with a points reward earns 5 points per booked seat for bookings created within the requested month.

A driver may publish a new trip only when the proposed trip has a valid time window and does not overlap with the driver’s existing trips. Two indirect trips posted by the same driver are considered overlapping by stops when they share at least one stop station, and stop-name comparison is case-sensitive.
Functional requirement:
1. Validate Booking Eligibility.
The system shall determine whether a customer can book seats on a trip. The trip must exist, the trip must still have enough available seats, the requested seats must not exceed the remaining seats, and the customer must not already hold another booking whose trip time overlaps on the same day. The booking time must be strictly earlier than the departure time by more than two hours, so a booking made exactly two hours before departure is rejected. When the booking is accepted, the trip seat count shall be reduced. Invalid inputs such as a null customer, null trip, or null booking date shall return `false`.

2. Calculate Discounted Trip Price.
The system shall calculate the final price of a booking after reward evaluation. A fixed 20 percent discount applies only when the customer owns a membership package containing the `DISCOUNTS` award and the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure. The returned amount shall keep one decimal place. When the customer, membership package, booking time, or reward condition is invalid or missing, the original trip price shall be returned.

3. Check Stop Overlap for Indirect Trips.
The system shall determine whether two indirect trips posted by the same driver share at least one common stop station. The comparison is case-sensitive. If either trip is null or one of the stop collections is empty, the result shall be `false`.

4. Compute Monthly Reward Points.
The system shall compute the reward points earned by a customer during a given month. Only customers whose membership package contains the `POINTS` award are eligible. Only bookings whose booking date falls inside the requested month shall be counted. Each booked seat contributes 5 points. Invalid inputs, missing membership packages, or unsupported rewards shall return `0`.

5. Validate Trip Posting Feasibility.
The system shall validate whether a driver can publish a new trip. The proposed trip must exist, its departure time and arrival time must be valid, and the departure time must be earlier than the arrival time. The new trip must not overlap with any existing trip of the driver. Completely identical time periods are conflicts, while adjacent boundaries where one trip ends exactly when another starts are allowed. Invalid inputs shall return `false`.
```

# Requirement
```text
Online Rideshare System (ORS) manages shared road trips between drivers and customers. Every user is identified by an id and also stores an email address and a phone number so that the platform can distinguish and contact the user.

A driver can publish trips. A trip records a departure station, an arrival station, the number of available seats, a departure date, a departure time, an arrival time, and a price. Trips can be direct or indirect. An indirect trip contains one or more stops, and each stop stores the name of its stop station.

A customer can create bookings for trips. A booking records the requested number of seats, the booking date, the related customer, and the related trip. A booking is valid only when the trip exists, enough seats are still available, the customer has no overlapping booking on the same day, and the booking is made more than two hours before the trip departure time. When a booking is accepted, the trip seat inventory must be reduced accordingly.

Customers may subscribe to a membership package. A membership package stores one or more rewards, and each reward is one of cashback, discounts, or points. A customer with a discount reward receives a 20 percent discount only when the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure. A customer with a points reward earns 5 points per booked seat for bookings created within the requested month.

A driver may publish a new trip only when the proposed trip has a valid time window and does not overlap with the driver’s existing trips. Two indirect trips posted by the same driver are considered overlapping by stops when they share at least one stop station, and stop-name comparison is case-sensitive.
Functional requirement:
1. Validate Booking Eligibility.
The system shall determine whether a customer can book seats on a trip. The trip must exist, the trip must still have enough available seats, the requested seats must not exceed the remaining seats, and the customer must not already hold another booking whose trip time overlaps on the same day. The booking time must be strictly earlier than the departure time by more than two hours, so a booking made exactly two hours before departure is rejected. When the booking is accepted, the trip seat count shall be reduced. Invalid inputs such as a null customer, null trip, or null booking date shall return `false`.

2. Calculate Discounted Trip Price.
The system shall calculate the final price of a booking after reward evaluation. A fixed 20 percent discount applies only when the customer owns a membership package containing the `DISCOUNTS` award and the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure. The returned amount shall keep one decimal place. When the customer, membership package, booking time, or reward condition is invalid or missing, the original trip price shall be returned.

3. Check Stop Overlap for Indirect Trips.
The system shall determine whether two indirect trips posted by the same driver share at least one common stop station. The comparison is case-sensitive. If either trip is null or one of the stop collections is empty, the result shall be `false`.

4. Compute Monthly Reward Points.
The system shall compute the reward points earned by a customer during a given month. Only customers whose membership package contains the `POINTS` award are eligible. Only bookings whose booking date falls inside the requested month shall be counted. Each booked seat contributes 5 points. Invalid inputs, missing membership packages, or unsupported rewards shall return `0`.

5. Validate Trip Posting Feasibility.
The system shall validate whether a driver can publish a new trip. The proposed trip must exist, its departure time and arrival time must be valid, and the departure time must be earlier than the arrival time. The new trip must not overlap with any existing trip of the driver. Completely identical time periods are conflicts, while adjacent boundaries where one trip ends exactly when another starts are allowed. Invalid inputs shall return `false`.
```

# Requirement
```text
Online Rideshare System (ORS) manages shared road trips between drivers and customers. Every user is identified by an id and also stores an email address and a phone number so that the platform can distinguish and contact the user.

A driver can publish trips. A trip records a departure station, an arrival station, the number of available seats, a departure date, a departure time, an arrival time, and a price. Trips can be direct or indirect. An indirect trip contains one or more stops, and each stop stores the name of its stop station.

A customer can create bookings for trips. A booking records the requested number of seats, the booking date, the related customer, and the related trip. A booking is valid only when the trip exists, enough seats are still available, the customer has no overlapping booking on the same day, and the booking is made more than two hours before the trip departure time. When a booking is accepted, the trip seat inventory must be reduced accordingly.

Customers may subscribe to a membership package. A membership package stores one or more rewards, and each reward is one of cashback, discounts, or points. A customer with a discount reward receives a 20 percent discount only when the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure. A customer with a points reward earns 5 points per booked seat for bookings created within the requested month.

A driver may publish a new trip only when the proposed trip has a valid time window and does not overlap with the driver’s existing trips. Two indirect trips posted by the same driver are considered overlapping by stops when they share at least one stop station, and stop-name comparison is case-sensitive.
Functional requirement:
1. Validate Booking Eligibility.
The system shall determine whether a customer can book seats on a trip. The trip must exist, the trip must still have enough available seats, the requested seats must not exceed the remaining seats, and the customer must not already hold another booking whose trip time overlaps on the same day. The booking time must be strictly earlier than the departure time by more than two hours, so a booking made exactly two hours before departure is rejected. When the booking is accepted, the trip seat count shall be reduced. Invalid inputs such as a null customer, null trip, or null booking date shall return `false`.

2. Calculate Discounted Trip Price.
The system shall calculate the final price of a booking after reward evaluation. A fixed 20 percent discount applies only when the customer owns a membership package containing the `DISCOUNTS` award and the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure. The returned amount shall keep one decimal place. When the customer, membership package, booking time, or reward condition is invalid or missing, the original trip price shall be returned.

3. Check Stop Overlap for Indirect Trips.
The system shall determine whether two indirect trips posted by the same driver share at least one common stop station. The comparison is case-sensitive. If either trip is null or one of the stop collections is empty, the result shall be `false`.

4. Compute Monthly Reward Points.
The system shall compute the reward points earned by a customer during a given month. Only customers whose membership package contains the `POINTS` award are eligible. Only bookings whose booking date falls inside the requested month shall be counted. Each booked seat contributes 5 points. Invalid inputs, missing membership packages, or unsupported rewards shall return `0`.

5. Validate Trip Posting Feasibility.
The system shall validate whether a driver can publish a new trip. The proposed trip must exist, its departure time and arrival time must be valid, and the departure time must be earlier than the arrival time. The new trip must not overlap with any existing trip of the driver. Completely identical time periods are conflicts, while adjacent boundaries where one trip ends exactly when another starts are allowed. Invalid inputs shall return `false`.
```

# Requirement
```text
Online Rideshare System (ORS) manages shared road trips between drivers and customers. Every user is identified by an id and also stores an email address and a phone number so that the platform can distinguish and contact the user.

A driver can publish trips. A trip records a departure station, an arrival station, the number of available seats, a departure date, a departure time, an arrival time, and a price. Trips can be direct or indirect. An indirect trip contains one or more stops, and each stop stores the name of its stop station.

A customer can create bookings for trips. A booking records the requested number of seats, the booking date, the related customer, and the related trip. A booking is valid only when the trip exists, enough seats are still available, the customer has no overlapping booking on the same day, and the booking is made more than two hours before the trip departure time. When a booking is accepted, the trip seat inventory must be reduced accordingly.

Customers may subscribe to a membership package. A membership package stores one or more rewards, and each reward is one of cashback, discounts, or points. A customer with a discount reward receives a 20 percent discount only when the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure. A customer with a points reward earns 5 points per booked seat for bookings created within the requested month.

A driver may publish a new trip only when the proposed trip has a valid time window and does not overlap with the driver’s existing trips. Two indirect trips posted by the same driver are considered overlapping by stops when they share at least one stop station, and stop-name comparison is case-sensitive.
Functional requirement:
1. Validate Booking Eligibility.
The system shall determine whether a customer can book seats on a trip. The trip must exist, the trip must still have enough available seats, the requested seats must not exceed the remaining seats, and the customer must not already hold another booking whose trip time overlaps on the same day. The booking time must be strictly earlier than the departure time by more than two hours, so a booking made exactly two hours before departure is rejected. When the booking is accepted, the trip seat count shall be reduced. Invalid inputs such as a null customer, null trip, or null booking date shall return `false`.

2. Calculate Discounted Trip Price.
The system shall calculate the final price of a booking after reward evaluation. A fixed 20 percent discount applies only when the customer owns a membership package containing the `DISCOUNTS` award and the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure. The returned amount shall keep one decimal place. When the customer, membership package, booking time, or reward condition is invalid or missing, the original trip price shall be returned.

3. Check Stop Overlap for Indirect Trips.
The system shall determine whether two indirect trips posted by the same driver share at least one common stop station. The comparison is case-sensitive. If either trip is null or one of the stop collections is empty, the result shall be `false`.

4. Compute Monthly Reward Points.
The system shall compute the reward points earned by a customer during a given month. Only customers whose membership package contains the `POINTS` award are eligible. Only bookings whose booking date falls inside the requested month shall be counted. Each booked seat contributes 5 points. Invalid inputs, missing membership packages, or unsupported rewards shall return `0`.

5. Validate Trip Posting Feasibility.
The system shall validate whether a driver can publish a new trip. The proposed trip must exist, its departure time and arrival time must be valid, and the departure time must be earlier than the arrival time. The new trip must not overlap with any existing trip of the driver. Completely identical time periods are conflicts, while adjacent boundaries where one trip ends exactly when another starts are allowed. Invalid inputs shall return `false`.
```

# Operation Specifications
Driver::canPostTrip
Summary: Validates whether a driver can publish a new trip. The trip must exist, have valid times, and not overlap with any existing trip of the driver.
Algorithm:
  1. If newtrip is null, return false.
  2. If newtrip.departureStation is null OR newtrip.arrivalStation is null OR newtrip.departureDate is null OR newtrip.departureTime is null OR newtrip.arrivalTime is null, return false.
  3. If newtrip.departureTime is not earlier than newtrip.arrivalTime (lexicographically or time comparison), return false.
  4. For each existingTrip in this.trips:
     - If existingTrip.isTimeConflicting(newtrip.departureTime, newtrip.arrivalTime) is true, return false.
  5. Return true.
Related Features: trips
Related Classes: Trip
Input: newtrip: Trip – the proposed trip to publish
Output: boolean – true if the trip can be published, false otherwise
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: None

Driver::checkStopOverlap
Summary: Determines whether two indirect trips posted by the same driver share at least one common stop station (case-sensitive).
Algorithm:
  1. If trip1 is null OR trip2 is null, return false.
  2. stops1 = trip1.getStopStations()
  3. stops2 = trip2.getStopStations()
  4. If stops1 is null OR stops2 is null OR stops1.isEmpty() OR stops2.isEmpty(), return false.
  5. For each station in stops1:
     - If stops2 contains station (case-sensitive), return true.
  6. Return false.
Related Features: trips
Related Classes: Trip
Input: trip1: Trip, trip2: Trip – the two trips to compare
Output: boolean – true if they share at least one stop station
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: None

  2. If currentMonth is null or invalid format, return 0.
  3. totalPoints = 0.
  4. For each booking in this.bookings:
     - If booking.customer == customer AND booking.isInMonth(currentMonth) is true:
       totalPoints = totalPoints + (booking.numberOfSeats * 5)
  5. Return totalPoints.

Related Classes: Booking

Trip::calculateDiscountedPrice
Summary: Calculates the final price of a booking after applying a 20% discount if the customer has a DISCOUNTS award and the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure.
Algorithm:
  1. If customer is null OR customer.membershipPackage is null OR customer.membershipPackage.hasAward(DISCOUNTS) is false, return this.price.
  2. If bookingTime is null OR format invalid, return this.price.
  3. If bookingTime is not at least 24 hours before this.departureDate + this.departureTime, return this.price.
  4. Return Math.round((this.price * 0.8) * 10.0) / 10.0.
Related Features: price, departureDate, departureTime
Related Classes: Customer, MembershipPackage, Award

Pre-condition: None

Trip::isTimeConflicting
Summary: Checks if a given time window conflicts with this trip's time window. Adjacent boundaries (one ends exactly when another starts) are allowed.
Algorithm:
  1. If newDepartureTime is null OR newArrivalTime is null, return false.
  2. If newDepartureTime is not before newArrivalTime, return false.
  3. If newDepartureTime is before this.departureTime AND newArrivalTime is before or equal to this.departureTime, return false.
  4. If newDepartureTime is after or equal to this.arrivalTime AND newArrivalTime is after this.arrivalTime, return false.
  5. Return true (there is an overlap).
Related Features: departureTime, arrivalTime
Related Classes: None
Input: newDepartureTime: String – departure time of the proposed trip; newArrivalTime: String – arrival time of the proposed trip
Output: boolean – true if there is a time conflict
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: None

Trip::bookSeats
Summary: Attempts to book a given number of seats on this trip.
Algorithm:
  1. If num <= 0, return false.
  2. If this.numberOfSeats < num, return false.
  3. this.numberOfSeats = this.numberOfSeats - num.
  4. Return true.
Related Features: numberOfSeats
Related Classes: None
Input: num: int – number of seats to book
Output: boolean – true if booking succeeded
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: If true, numberOfSeats is reduced by num.

# Requirement
```text
Online Rideshare System (ORS) manages shared road trips between drivers and customers. Every user is identified by an id and also stores an email address and a phone number so that the platform can distinguish and contact the user.

A driver can publish trips. A trip records a departure station, an arrival station, the number of available seats, a departure date, a departure time, an arrival time, and a price. Trips can be direct or indirect. An indirect trip contains one or more stops, and each stop stores the name of its stop station.

A customer can create bookings for trips. A booking records the requested number of seats, the booking date, the related customer, and the related trip. A booking is valid only when the trip exists, enough seats are still available, the customer has no overlapping booking on the same day, and the booking is made more than two hours before the trip departure time. When a booking is accepted, the trip seat inventory must be reduced accordingly.

Customers may subscribe to a membership package. A membership package stores one or more rewards, and each reward is one of cashback, discounts, or points. A customer with a discount reward receives a 20 percent discount only when the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure. A customer with a points reward earns 5 points per booked seat for bookings created within the requested month.

A driver may publish a new trip only when the proposed trip has a valid time window and does not overlap with the driver’s existing trips. Two indirect trips posted by the same driver are considered overlapping by stops when they share at least one stop station, and stop-name comparison is case-sensitive.
Functional requirement:
1. Validate Booking Eligibility.
The system shall determine whether a customer can book seats on a trip. The trip must exist, the trip must still have enough available seats, the requested seats must not exceed the remaining seats, and the customer must not already hold another booking whose trip time overlaps on the same day. The booking time must be strictly earlier than the departure time by more than two hours, so a booking made exactly two hours before departure is rejected. When the booking is accepted, the trip seat count shall be reduced. Invalid inputs such as a null customer, null trip, or null booking date shall return `false`.

2. Calculate Discounted Trip Price.
The system shall calculate the final price of a booking after reward evaluation. A fixed 20 percent discount applies only when the customer owns a membership package containing the `DISCOUNTS` award and the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure. The returned amount shall keep one decimal place. When the customer, membership package, booking time, or reward condition is invalid or missing, the original trip price shall be returned.

3. Check Stop Overlap for Indirect Trips.
The system shall determine whether two indirect trips posted by the same driver share at least one common stop station. The comparison is case-sensitive. If either trip is null or one of the stop collections is empty, the result shall be `false`.

4. Compute Monthly Reward Points.
The system shall compute the reward points earned by a customer during a given month. Only customers whose membership package contains the `POINTS` award are eligible. Only bookings whose booking date falls inside the requested month shall be counted. Each booked seat contributes 5 points. Invalid inputs, missing membership packages, or unsupported rewards shall return `0`.

5. Validate Trip Posting Feasibility.
The system shall validate whether a driver can publish a new trip. The proposed trip must exist, its departure time and arrival time must be valid, and the departure time must be earlier than the arrival time. The new trip must not overlap with any existing trip of the driver. Completely identical time periods are conflicts, while adjacent boundaries where one trip ends exactly when another starts are allowed. Invalid inputs shall return `false`.
```

Related Classes: Booking

Trip::calculateDiscountedPrice

Algorithm:

  2. If bookingTime is null OR format invalid, return this.price.
  3. If bookingTime is not at least 24 hours before this.departureDate + this.departureTime, return this.price.

Trip::isTimeConflicting
Summary: Checks if a given time window conflicts with this trip's time window. Adjacent boundaries (one ends exactly when another starts) are allowed.
Algorithm:
  1. If newDepartureTime is null OR newArrivalTime is null, return false.
  2. If newDepartureTime is not before newArrivalTime, return false.
  3. If newDepartureTime is before this.departureTime AND newArrivalTime is before or equal to this.departureTime, return false.
  4. If newDepartureTime is after or equal to this.arrivalTime AND newArrivalTime is after this.arrivalTime, return false.
  5. Return true (there is an overlap).
Related Features: departureTime, arrivalTime
Related Classes: None
Input: newDepartureTime: String – departure time of the proposed trip; newArrivalTime: String – arrival time of the proposed trip
Output: boolean – true if there is a time conflict
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: None

Trip::bookSeats
Summary: Attempts to book a given number of seats on this trip.
Algorithm:
  1. If num <= 0, return false.
  2. If this.numberOfSeats < num, return false.
  3. this.numberOfSeats = this.numberOfSeats - num.
  4. Return true.
Related Features: numberOfSeats
Related Classes: None
Input: num: int – number of seats to book
Output: boolean – true if booking succeeded
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: If true, numberOfSeats is reduced by num.

# Requirement
```text
Online Rideshare System (ORS) manages shared road trips between drivers and customers. Every user is identified by an id and also stores an email address and a phone number so that the platform can distinguish and contact the user.

A driver can publish trips. A trip records a departure station, an arrival station, the number of available seats, a departure date, a departure time, an arrival time, and a price. Trips can be direct or indirect. An indirect trip contains one or more stops, and each stop stores the name of its stop station.

A customer can create bookings for trips. A booking records the requested number of seats, the booking date, the related customer, and the related trip. A booking is valid only when the trip exists, enough seats are still available, the customer has no overlapping booking on the same day, and the booking is made more than two hours before the trip departure time. When a booking is accepted, the trip seat inventory must be reduced accordingly.

Customers may subscribe to a membership package. A membership package stores one or more rewards, and each reward is one of cashback, discounts, or points. A customer with a discount reward receives a 20 percent discount only when the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure. A customer with a points reward earns 5 points per booked seat for bookings created within the requested month.

A driver may publish a new trip only when the proposed trip has a valid time window and does not overlap with the driver’s existing trips. Two indirect trips posted by the same driver are considered overlapping by stops when they share at least one stop station, and stop-name comparison is case-sensitive.
Functional requirement:
1. Validate Booking Eligibility.
The system shall determine whether a customer can book seats on a trip. The trip must exist, the trip must still have enough available seats, the requested seats must not exceed the remaining seats, and the customer must not already hold another booking whose trip time overlaps on the same day. The booking time must be strictly earlier than the departure time by more than two hours, so a booking made exactly two hours before departure is rejected. When the booking is accepted, the trip seat count shall be reduced. Invalid inputs such as a null customer, null trip, or null booking date shall return `false`.

2. Calculate Discounted Trip Price.
The system shall calculate the final price of a booking after reward evaluation. A fixed 20 percent discount applies only when the customer owns a membership package containing the `DISCOUNTS` award and the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure. The returned amount shall keep one decimal place. When the customer, membership package, booking time, or reward condition is invalid or missing, the original trip price shall be returned.

3. Check Stop Overlap for Indirect Trips.
The system shall determine whether two indirect trips posted by the same driver share at least one common stop station. The comparison is case-sensitive. If either trip is null or one of the stop collections is empty, the result shall be `false`.

4. Compute Monthly Reward Points.
The system shall compute the reward points earned by a customer during a given month. Only customers whose membership package contains the `POINTS` award are eligible. Only bookings whose booking date falls inside the requested month shall be counted. Each booked seat contributes 5 points. Invalid inputs, missing membership packages, or unsupported rewards shall return `0`.

5. Validate Trip Posting Feasibility.
The system shall validate whether a driver can publish a new trip. The proposed trip must exist, its departure time and arrival time must be valid, and the departure time must be earlier than the arrival time. The new trip must not overlap with any existing trip of the driver. Completely identical time periods are conflicts, while adjacent boundaries where one trip ends exactly when another starts are allowed. Invalid inputs shall return `false`.
```

# Operation Specifications
Booking::overlapsWith
Summary: Checks if this booking's trip time window overlaps with the given trip's time window.
Algorithm:
  1. If trip is null, return false.
  2. If this.trip.departureDate != trip.departureDate, return false (different days).
  3. If this.trip.departureTime is before trip.arrivalTime AND trip.departureTime is before this.trip.arrivalTime, return true.
  4. Return false.
Related Features: trip, trip.departureDate, trip.departureTime, trip.arrivalTime
Related Classes: Trip
Input: trip: Trip – the trip to compare against
Output: boolean – true if time windows overlap
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: None

Booking::updateTripSeats
Summary: Reduces the trip's available seats by the number of booked seats.
Algorithm:
  1. trip.numberOfSeats = trip.numberOfSeats - this.numberOfSeats.
Related Features: trip, numberOfSeats, trip.numberOfSeats
Related Classes: Trip
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: The booking must be eligible and accepted.
Post-condition: trip.numberOfSeats is reduced by this.numberOfSeats.

Booking::isBookingEligible
Summary: Determines whether a customer can book seats on a trip. The trip must exist, have enough available seats, the customer must not have an overlapping booking on the same day, and the booking must be made more than two hours before departure.
Algorithm:
  1. If customer is null OR trip is null OR bookingDate is null, return false.
  2. If trip.numberOfSeats < numberOfSeats, return false.
  3. If trip.departureDate + trip.departureTime - bookingDate <= 2 hours, return false.
  4. For each existingBooking in customer.bookings:
     - If existingBooking.trip.departureDate == trip.departureDate AND existingBooking.overlapsWith(trip) is true, return false.
  5. trip.numberOfSeats = trip.numberOfSeats - numberOfSeats.
  6. Return true.
Related Features: numberOfSeats, customer, trip, bookingDate
Related Classes: Customer, Trip
Input: customer: Customer – the customer making the booking; trip: Trip – the trip to book; numberOfSeats: int – number of seats requested; bookingDate: EDate – the date/time of booking
Output: boolean – true if booking is eligible
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: If true, trip.numberOfSeats is reduced by numberOfSeats.

Booking::isInMonth
Summary: Checks if this booking's booking date falls within the specified month.
Algorithm:
  1. If bookingDate is null OR month is null, return false.
  2. Extract year and month from bookingDate.
  3. Extract year and month from the given month string.
  4. Return true if they match, false otherwise.
Related Features: bookingDate
Related Classes: None
Input: month: String – month in format "yyyy-MM"
Output: boolean – true if booking is in the specified month
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: None

# Requirement
```text
Online Rideshare System (ORS) manages shared road trips between drivers and customers. Every user is identified by an id and also stores an email address and a phone number so that the platform can distinguish and contact the user.

A driver can publish trips. A trip records a departure station, an arrival station, the number of available seats, a departure date, a departure time, an arrival time, and a price. Trips can be direct or indirect. An indirect trip contains one or more stops, and each stop stores the name of its stop station.

A customer can create bookings for trips. A booking records the requested number of seats, the booking date, the related customer, and the related trip. A booking is valid only when the trip exists, enough seats are still available, the customer has no overlapping booking on the same day, and the booking is made more than two hours before the trip departure time. When a booking is accepted, the trip seat inventory must be reduced accordingly.

Customers may subscribe to a membership package. A membership package stores one or more rewards, and each reward is one of cashback, discounts, or points. A customer with a discount reward receives a 20 percent discount only when the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure. A customer with a points reward earns 5 points per booked seat for bookings created within the requested month.

A driver may publish a new trip only when the proposed trip has a valid time window and does not overlap with the driver’s existing trips. Two indirect trips posted by the same driver are considered overlapping by stops when they share at least one stop station, and stop-name comparison is case-sensitive.
Functional requirement:
1. Validate Booking Eligibility.
The system shall determine whether a customer can book seats on a trip. The trip must exist, the trip must still have enough available seats, the requested seats must not exceed the remaining seats, and the customer must not already hold another booking whose trip time overlaps on the same day. The booking time must be strictly earlier than the departure time by more than two hours, so a booking made exactly two hours before departure is rejected. When the booking is accepted, the trip seat count shall be reduced. Invalid inputs such as a null customer, null trip, or null booking date shall return `false`.

2. Calculate Discounted Trip Price.
The system shall calculate the final price of a booking after reward evaluation. A fixed 20 percent discount applies only when the customer owns a membership package containing the `DISCOUNTS` award and the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure. The returned amount shall keep one decimal place. When the customer, membership package, booking time, or reward condition is invalid or missing, the original trip price shall be returned.

3. Check Stop Overlap for Indirect Trips.
The system shall determine whether two indirect trips posted by the same driver share at least one common stop station. The comparison is case-sensitive. If either trip is null or one of the stop collections is empty, the result shall be `false`.

4. Compute Monthly Reward Points.
The system shall compute the reward points earned by a customer during a given month. Only customers whose membership package contains the `POINTS` award are eligible. Only bookings whose booking date falls inside the requested month shall be counted. Each booked seat contributes 5 points. Invalid inputs, missing membership packages, or unsupported rewards shall return `0`.

5. Validate Trip Posting Feasibility.
The system shall validate whether a driver can publish a new trip. The proposed trip must exist, its departure time and arrival time must be valid, and the departure time must be earlier than the arrival time. The new trip must not overlap with any existing trip of the driver. Completely identical time periods are conflicts, while adjacent boundaries where one trip ends exactly when another starts are allowed. Invalid inputs shall return `false`.
```

Implementation:
```java
public int computeMonthlyRewardPoints(final String currentMonth)
{
    if (currentMonth == null || currentMonth.isEmpty())
    {
      return 0;
    }
    MembershipPackage mp = getMembershipPackage();
    if (mp == null || !mp.hasAward(Award.POINTS))
    {
      return 0;
    }
    int totalPoints = 0;
    for (Booking booking : getBookings())
    {
      if (booking.isInMonth(currentMonth))
      {
        totalPoints = totalPoints + (booking.getNumberOfSeats() * 5);
      }
    }
    return totalPoints;
}
```

For `bookTrip`:
```java
public void bookTrip(final Trip trip, final int numberOfSeats)
{
    if (trip == null || numberOfSeats <= 0)
    {
      return;
    }
    Booking booking = RideshareFactory.eINSTANCE.createBooking();
    booking.setBookingDate(new Date());
    booking.setNumberOfSeats(numberOfSeats);
    booking.setCustomer(this);
    booking.setTrip(trip);
    if (booking.isBookingEligible())
```

```java
   * Summary: Calculates the final price of a booking after applying a 20% discount if the customer has a DISCOUNTS award and the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure. If conditions are not met, returns the original price with one decimal place.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If customer is null OR customer.membershipPackage is null OR customer.membershipPackage.hasAward(DISCOUNTS) is false, return this.price.
   *   2. If bookingTime is null OR format invalid, return this.price.
   *   3. If bookingTime is not at least 24 hours before this.departureDate + this.departureTime, return this.price.
   *   4. Return Math.round((this.price * 0.8) * 10.0) / 10.0.
   * Related Features: price, departureDate, departureTime
   * Related Classes: Customer, MembershipPackage, Award
   * Input: customer: Customer – the customer making the booking; bookingTime: String – the booking date/time in format "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm"
   * Output: double – the discounted price with one decimal place, or original price with one decimal place if conditions not met
   * Pre-condition: None
   * Post-condition: If discount is applied, the returned value is 80% of the original price rounded to one decimal place; otherwise original price is returned unchanged.
```

   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public double calculateDiscountedPrice(final Customer customer, final String bookingTime)
  {
    // Check eligibility: customer, membership package, and DISCOUNTS award
    if (customer == null || customer.getMembershipPackage() == null || !customer.getMembershipPackage().hasAward(Award.DISCOUNTS))
    {
      return this.price;
    }

    // Check bookingTime validity
    if (bookingTime == null)
    {
      return this.price;
    }

    // Parse bookingTime as "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm"
    java.text.SimpleDateFormat sdf = new java.text.SimpleDateFormat("yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm");
    sdf.setLenient(false);
    java.util.Date bookingDate;
    try
    {
      bookingDate = sdf.parse(bookingTime);
    }
    catch (java.text.ParseException e)
    {
      return this.price;
    }

    // Check if departureDate + departureTime is valid
    if (this.departureDate == null || this.departureTime == null)
    {
      return this.price;
    }

    // Parse departure date and time to create a full departure datetime
    java.text.SimpleDateFormat dateSdf = new java.text.SimpleDateFormat("yyyy-MM-dd");
    String departureDateStr = dateSdf.format(this.departureDate);
    String departureDateTimeStr = departureDateStr + " " + this.departureTime;
    java.util.Date departureDateTime;
    try
    {
      departureDateTime = sdf.parse(departureDateTimeStr);
    }
    catch (java.text.ParseException e)
    {
      return this.price;
    }

    // Check if bookingTime is at least 24 hours before departure
    long diffMillis = departureDateTime.getTime() - bookingDate.getTime();
    long twentyFourHoursInMillis = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000L;
    if (diffMillis < twentyFourHoursInMillis)
    {
      return this.price;
    }

    // Apply 20% discount and round to one decimal place
    return Math.round((this.price * 0.8) * 10.0) / 10.0;

    java.text.SimpleDateFormat monthSdf = new java.text.SimpleDateFormat("yyyy-MM");

   *   5. Return true (there is an overlap).
   * Related Features: departureTime, arrivalTime
   * Related Classes: None
   * Input: newDepartureTime: String – departure time of the proposed trip; newArrivalTime: String – arrival time of the proposed trip
   * Output: boolean – true if there is a time conflict (including exact overlap), false if no conflict or invalid input

   * Post-condition: None
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"

  {

    }
    if (newDepartureTime.compareTo(newArrivalTime) >= 0)
    {
      return false;
    }
    if (newDepartureTime.compareTo(this.departureTime) < 0 && newArrivalTime.compareTo(this.departureTime) <= 0)
    {
      return false;
    }
    if (newDepartureTime.compareTo(this.arrivalTime) >= 0 && newArrivalTime.compareTo(this.arrivalTime) > 0)
    {
      return false;
    }
    return true;
  }

public boolean isBookingEligible()
{
  // 1. If customer is null OR trip is null OR bookingDate is null, return false.
  if (getCustomer() == null || getTrip() == null || getBookingDate() == null) {
    return false;
  }
  // 2. If trip.numberOfSeats < numberOfSeats, return false.
  if (getTrip().getNumberOfSeats() < getNumberOfSeats()) {
    return false;
  }
  // 3. If (trip.departureDateTime - bookingDate) < 2 hours, return false.
  try {
    SimpleDateFormat dateFormat = new SimpleDateFormat("yyyy-MM-dd");
    SimpleDateFormat dateTimeFormat = new SimpleDateFormat("yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm");
    String datePart = dateFormat.format(getTrip().getDepartureDate());
    String timePart = getTrip().getDepartureTime();
    Date departureDateTime = dateTimeFormat.parse(datePart + " " + timePart);
    long diffMs = departureDateTime.getTime() - getBookingDate().getTime();
    if (diffMs < 2 * 60 * 60 * 1000L) {
      return false;
    }
  } catch (ParseException e) {
    return false;
  }
  // 4. For each existingBooking in customer.bookings
  for (Booking existingBooking : getCustomer().getBookings()) {
    if (existingBooking.overlapsWith(getTrip())) {
      return false;
    }
  }
  // 5. trip.bookSeats(numberOfSeats)
  getTrip().bookSeats(getNumberOfSeats());
  // 6. Return true
  return true;
}

public boolean overlapsWith(final Trip trip)
{
  // 1. If trip is null, return false.
  if (trip == null) {
    return false;
  }
  // 2. If this.trip.departureDate != trip.departureDate, return false (different days).
  if (!getTrip().getDepartureDate().equals(trip.getDepartureDate())) {
    return false;
  }
  // 3. If this.trip.departureTime is before trip.arrivalTime AND trip.departureTime is before this.trip.arrivalTime, return true.
  try {
    SimpleDateFormat timeFormat = new SimpleDateFormat("HH:mm");
    Date thisDepartureTime = timeFormat.parse(getTrip().getDepartureTime());
    Date thisArrivalTime = timeFormat.parse(getTrip().getArrivalTime());
    Date otherDepartureTime = timeFormat.parse(trip.getDepartureTime());
    Date otherArrivalTime = timeFormat.parse(trip.getArrivalTime());
    if (thisDepartureTime.before(otherArrivalTime) && otherDepartureTime.before(thisArrivalTime)) {
      return true;
    }
  } catch (ParseException e) {
    return false;
  }
  // 4. Return false.
  return false;
}

    getTrip().setNumberOfSeats(getTrip().getNumberOfSeats() - getNumberOfSeats());
  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Checks if this booking's trip time window overlaps with the given trip's time window.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If trip is null, return false.
   *   2. If this.trip.departureDate != trip.departureDate, return false (different days).
   *   3. If this.trip.departureTime is before trip.arrivalTime AND trip.departureTime is before this.trip.arrivalTime, return true.
   *   4. Return false.
   * Related Features: trip, trip.departureDate, trip.departureTime, trip.arrivalTime
   * Related Classes: Trip
   * Input: trip: Trip – the trip to compare against
   * Output: boolean – true if time windows overlap
   * Pre-condition: None
   * Post-condition: None
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public boolean overlapsWith(final Trip trip)
  {
    // 1. If trip is null, return false.
    if (trip == null) {
      return false;
    }
    // 2. If this.trip.departureDate != trip.departureDate, return false (different days).
    if (!getTrip().getDepartureDate().equals(trip.getDepartureDate())) {
      return false;
    }
    // 3. If this.trip.departureTime is before trip.arrivalTime AND
    //    trip.departureTime is before this.trip.arrivalTime, return true.
    try {
      SimpleDateFormat timeFormat = new SimpleDateFormat("HH:mm");
      Date thisDepartureTime = timeFormat.parse(getTrip().getDepartureTime());
      Date thisArrivalTime = timeFormat.parse(getTrip().getArrivalTime());
      Date otherDepartureTime = timeFormat.parse(trip.getDepartureTime());
      Date otherArrivalTime = timeFormat.parse(trip.getArrivalTime());
      if (thisDepartureTime.before(otherArrivalTime) && otherDepartureTime.before(thisArrivalTime)) {
        return true;
      }
    } catch (ParseException e) {
      return false;
    }
    // 4. Return false.
    return false;
  }

  /**

   * @generated NOT

  public boolean isInMonth(final String month)
  {
    // 1. If bookingDate is null OR month is null, return false.

      return false;
    }
    // 2. Extract year and month from bookingDate.
    // 3. Extract year and month from the given month string.
    // 4. Return true if they match, false otherwise.

      String bookingMonth = sdf.format(getBookingDate());
      return bookingMonth.equals(month);
    } catch (Exception e) {
      return false;
    }
  }
